label: mid-input t/k/o/2/g/y (first occurrence) after a sequence starting with i/f/s/1
explanation: Fires only during the original input phase, essentially never at the delimiter or during copying, and mostly at positions 2-6 (peak at t=3-5). It is token-selective: t, k, o, 2, g and y as the current input carry about 94% of activation mass, and about 92% of mass is on the first occurrence of that token. Whether these tokens fire depends strongly on prefix context. Activations are larger and more frequent when the sequence begins with i, f, s or 1 (rates 2.6-4.3x for first_tok). The top examples nearly all start with f f, f s, i i or 1 f. A preceding g also helps. With no prefix condition, the token+position predicate reaches 86% mass recall but only 13% precision. The prefix condition raises precision to about 32% at about 63% mass recall, so the context dependence is only partly captured, and it looks like a graded function of the hidden state. It does not fire on t=0, on other letters such as w/q/l/e/r, on repeated occurrences, or in the copy phase.
